$comment: THE single source of truth for who may change what. Read by scripts/memory_guard.py (local pre-commit AND CI). Two independent axes: LEVEL (what kind of knowledge — decides who may change it and whether the change cascades) and TIER (how significant — decides whether it is worth storing at all, and in how much detail). Editing this file requires the `owner` role plus a CODEOWNERS review. JSON, not YAML, so it parses with the standard library on every machine with zero dependencies.

enforcement.$comment: mode=direct: agents' end-of-turn syncs push straight to the default branch (right before branch protection exists). mode=pr: the sync pushes each person's notes to their own branch memory/<who> and keeps one pull request open for it (sync-memory.py, read from the trusted HEAD policy); in direct mode a push refused by a protected branch falls back to the same. auto_merge_levels: levels memory-gate may merge without a person (it enables GitHub auto-merge; CODEOWNERS then names no reviewer for those levels). Switch mode to `pr` the day you protect main; add L0 here only after the gate has been proven on GitHub.
enforcement.$comment_containment: Empty by default: nothing merges without review until an owner adds a level after proving the gate on GitHub (RUNBOOK phase 4).

levels.$comment: The core of the model. A note declares its level in frontmatter (`level: L0`). The guard also infers the level from the path and FAILS if the declaration and the path disagree — so a note cannot smuggle strategy into the code tier.

L0.label: observation
L0.what: How the system actually behaves right now. Code-level facts, non-obvious gotchas, environment quirks, 'we tried X and it failed because Y', a component's real responsibility, a corrected assumption.
examples: the nightly export runs in UTC, not local time, so dates near midnight shift a day
uv tool install basic-memory fails on Python < 3.12; pass --python 3.12
Kiro ignores symlinked skills, so the copies must be regenerated

L1.label: project-planning
L1.what: How ONE project is planned and built: its scope, milestones, sequencing, project-level architecture and the decisions behind it.
examples: the product stores uploads in object storage, not on the app servers (a decision record)
Single sign-on is P0 and passing the security review is its exit criterion
The export step lives in export.py; legacy_export.py is superseded
L1.storage: full note with rationale, reviewed before merge

L2.label: ideation-and-strategy
L2.what: What we are building and why, across projects. Product thesis, company architecture, vendor and tooling strategy, conventions everyone follows, ownership. The ideological layer: changing it changes how every project should think.
examples: Background jobs run in the cheapest region that meets the latency target
One cloud provider is the platform of record; a second is priced as a hedge, not planned
Support response time is a product promise, not a cost line
L2.review: one steward who is not the author
L2.storage: full note with rationale and alternatives, reviewed before merge

L3.label: governance
L3.what: The rules of the memory system itself: roles, access, the agent rulebook, hooks, CI, the scripts hooks execute.
examples: What the Stop hook runs on every teammate's machine
L3.review: one owner who is not the author
L3.storage: ADR required for any rule change

cascade.$comment: What 'a planning change updates the entire context' means mechanically. When a note at L1/L2/L3 changes, scripts/memory_guard.py walks the RELATION GRAPH (the [[wikilinks]] in ## Relations) outward from it and stamps every dependent note with `review_needed`. Agents that later read a stamped note must say so in their one-line memory report and prefer the changed note. A steward clears the stamp by re-reading the dependent and removing the field, or by updating it.
cascade.$relation_comment: Only DEPENDENCY relations cascade. `relates_to` is deliberately absent: it means 'see also', every note has several, and following it flagged every note in testing — a review list that includes everything is a review list nobody works. If a note genuinely depends on another, say `depends_on` or `implements`.
cascade.$max_comment: Above this, the change is too central to review note-by-note: the cascade reports the set and asks a human to scope it rather than stamping everything.

people.$comment: handle = the short id used in a note's `author:` frontmatter. function (pm | eng | design | ops) only picks an agent's STARTING context mode; the ask always overrides it. restricted_read allows an agent acting for this person to load confidentiality:restricted notes; the real fence is still GitHub access to the restricted submodule. email MUST match that person's `git config user.email`, or the guard cannot stamp attribution for them. github = their GitHub login, used by CODEOWNERS and the CI attribution check. A person's role is their MAXIMUM; `projects` narrows where a maintainer's L1 rights apply.

roles.$comment: Ordered least to most privileged; each inherits the one before it. `agent` is not a person — it is the capability an AI agent runs with, deliberately the narrowest, regardless of who is driving it. An owner driving Claude Code still writes as `agent` for that turn: the human's rights apply when the human commits, not when their agent does.

agent.description: Any AI agent. Records observations; may never change canon, only propose.

reader.description: Read-only access to every tier except `restricted`.

contributor.description: Every engineer. Writes observations freely; proposes everything above.

maintainer.description: Owns named projects; changes planning for those projects only.

steward.description: Custodian of company canon: strategy, architecture, conventions.

owner.description: May change the rules themselves. Smallest group: these paths execute code on every teammate's machine.

paths.$comment: Level of each path. First match wins, most specific first. `bot` means only the GitHub Action identity writes it. Unlisted paths fall through to `default`.

rules.reason: changing the rules is the highest privilege in the system

sensitivity.$comment: Declared per note as `confidentiality:` in frontmatter. The guard enforces that a note's declared tier matches where it lives.

open.description: Safe to share outside the company.

internal.description: Default. Visible to everyone with access to this private repo; agents read it freely.

restricted.description: Commercially or legally sensitive: unsigned contract terms, security findings, anything under NDA that the whole team is not cleared for. NOT stored in this repo. It lives in a separate private repo mounted at context/restricted/ as a git submodule, so access is a GitHub repository permission — the only access control here that is genuinely enforced rather than merely requested. Teammates without access do not receive the files, and their Basic Memory indexes nothing there.

never_store.$comment: Not a tier. These never enter any repo, at any sensitivity, at any level. The guard blocks them by pattern and CI re-checks.

protocol.$comment: How agents load context (ADR-004). Read by scripts/mem.py. Order: who -> core -> resolve -> mode scope -> receipt -> plan -> execute -> write back. Scope is DIRECTIONAL: upstream = what a note relies on (its dependency edges), downstream = what relies on it. Undirected traversal is never used: at 3,020 notes, 3 hops of any link reached p95 333 notes; 2 directed hops stayed at p95 8-12.
protocol.$comment_extra_symptoms: Regular expressions for how bug reports in YOUR domain describe a symptom, added to mem.py's generic list (has no, missing, wrong, stuck, times out, too slow, ...). An ask with no intent word that matches one is read as debug. Example for a web app: ["\\bspins forever\\b", "\\b404\\b", "\\blogged out\\b"].
protocol.$comment_ask_on_guess: When mem load cannot tell the kind of task (no intent word, no symptom) or the feature, it asks the person with ranked options instead of loading a guess. false: load the best guess and mark it A GUESS in the receipt.
protocol.$comment_code_root: where features' covers: globs resolve, relative to the repo root. '.' = this repo (cairn's features cover its own scripts). MEMORY_CODE_ROOT overrides it.

publication.$comment: What the PUBLIC build of web/ may show. Separate from `sensitivity` because that governs the repository and this governs a URL anyone with the link can open. A note's one-line summary is the first sentence of the note, which for a strategy note is the strategy: publishing it undoes the redaction it sits beside. So summaries are published only for the levels listed here, plus any note explicitly marked `confidentiality: open`.

significance.$comment: The SECOND, independent axis: is this worth storing at all, and in how much detail? Level answers WHO and WHERE; significance answers WHETHER. Full rubric with worked examples: governance/SIGNIFICANCE.md.

A.label: decision
A.stored: full note with rationale and alternatives

$comment_instance: false in the Cairn template. `scripts/init.py` fills in the owner and sets this true; the memory-gate, cascade, changelog and atlas workflows only run on an initialized instance.
